samples.summary: The 'declines to snap when the endpoints cannot be ordered' test passes for the wrong reason - it cannot fail if the ordering guard is deleted
samples.evidence: The fixture builds `inCell` but only puts `other` into the doc (`makeDoc([other])`). `Doc.findBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:221) returns undefined for `inCell.id`, so `startBlock`/`startRun` are undefined and `expandRangeForLinks` returns the same object regardless of `anchorComesFirst`. Removing the `if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return undefined;` branch (then -1 < 0 makes anchorFirst true) still leaves both runs undefined, so the function hits `if (!startRun && !endRun) return range;` and the test still passes. The guard it is named for - the one preventing wrong-direction expansion that *shrinks* a real selection - has no test that can fail.

samples.summary: The `tableCellRange` skip test uses a collapsed range, so the collapsed early-return already satisfies it; the tableCellRange guard is untested

samples.summary: No test covers the pointer-gesture wiring of link snapping (setSnappedRange / rawAnchor) - drag and shift+click behaviour is only unit-tested at the pure-function level
samples.evidence: `expandRangeForLinks` is thoroughly unit-tested in link-run.test.ts, but nothing exercises `TextEditor.setSnappedRange`, its two mousedown call sites, or `updateDragSelection`. The whole stated rationale for `rawAnchor` - that dragging back out of a link un-snaps instead of ratcheting, and that shift+click re-extends from the raw anchor - has no test. selection-raw-anchor.test.ts only asserts that `setRange` nulls a field the test itself assigned, which is coverage of a one-line assignment, not of the ratchet behaviour it documents. Pointer-driven tests are feasible here: packages/docs/test/view/cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts:190 dispatches real `mousedown` events at canvas coordinates. A wiring mistake (rawAnchor not set on the drag-start path, snapping applied where the anchor was deliberately rewritten) would ship with a green suite and change selection behaviour users see on every drag over a link.
searchedFor: grep rawAnchor|expandRangeForLinks|setSnappedRange across repo (only src + the two test files)

finding.evidence: The fixture builds `inCell` but only puts `other` into the doc (`makeDoc([other])`). `Doc.findBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:221) returns undefined for `inCell.id`, so `startBlock`/`startRun` are undefined and `expandRangeForLinks` returns the same object regardless of `anchorComesFirst`. verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The test 'declines to snap when the endpoints cannot be ordered' (link-run.test.ts:314-329) builds `inCell` but never adds it to the doc (`makeDoc([other])`). With the guard at link-run.ts:104 present, `expandRangeForLinks` returns the same `range` object at line 143. With the guard removed, `getBlockIndex` returns -1 (document.ts:271-273) so `anchorFirst` becomes true, but `doc.findBlock(inCell.id)` is undefined (document.ts:221-231; the block is in neither the block list nor any table cell), and `other` has no link, so both runs are undefined and line 152 returns the identical `range` — `toBe(range)` still passes. The assertion therefore cannot fail if the ordering guard is deleted, and no other test covers it (the only other file referencing expandRangeForLinks, selection-raw-anchor.test.ts, tests rawAnchor clearing). Since wrong-direction expansion silently shrinks a real cross-block selection (dropping selected characters), this is fake coverage over a user-visible behavior: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.evidence: The fixture's anchor and focus are both offset 8, so `expandRangeForLinks` returns `range` from the collapsed-range guard before it ever matters that `range.tableCellRange` is set. `expect(expandRangeForLinks(doc, cellRange)).toBe(cellRange)` therefore passes even if `if (range.tableCellRange) return range;` is deleted. verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The test at packages/docs/test/view/link-run.test.ts:270-282 builds a range whose anchor and focus are both {blockId: id, offset: 8} — a collapsed range in a single block. In expandRangeForLinks (packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:133-140) the tableCellRange guard (line 134) and the collapsed guard (lines 135-140) both `return range`, returning the identical object, so `expect(...).toBe(cellRange)` passes even with line 134 deleted. The assertion therefore holds regardless of whether the tableCellRange guard exists, making it vacuous coverage for the behavior it names. Grepping all of packages/docs/test shows expandRangeForLinks is only called from link-run.test.ts, and no test anywhere passes a non-collapsed tableCellRange (the shape a real cross-cell drag produces via TextEditor.setSnappedRange at text-editor.ts:2368-2374). So the guard has no meaningful test; offset mangling in cell-range mode would ship green. Squarely in the test-adequacy lane (vacuous test presented as coverage for a behavior in this diff), and the failure mode is a user-visible selection/offset corruption during table cell drags, so major is appropriate.

verdict.reason: The guard exists exactly as described (docs-link-popover.tsx:52 state, :88 and :128 setters, :120 reset, :150-156 early return) and nothing tests it. No test file in the repo imports or renders DocsLinkPopover: grep for 'DocsLinkPopover', 'docs-link-popover', and the input's aria-label 'Link URL' match only the source plus docs-view.tsx:24 and markdown/.agent-review artifacts. The getLinkAtCursor hits in packages/docs/test are editor-level contract/tie-break tests (text-box-editor.test.ts:339-347, edit-link-in-place.test.ts:232 and :261-285, link-run.test.ts:85); they cannot fail if the popover forgets to consult the guard, because the composition (editingExistingLink && !getLinkAtCursor()) lives solely in the component. The change's own plan corroborates the omission: the todo checks off 'Guard the popover' at lines 28-31 while its Tests section (lines 66-76) lists only packages/docs/test/view files. Component testing is available in this package (docs-format-painter-toggle.test.tsx:10 imports render/fireEvent from @testing-library/react, alongside docs-context-menu/docs-find-bar-read-only/docs-page-setup-dialog tests), so this is a plain gap rather than an infrastructure limit. Severity major: if the guard is mis-wired, Apply silently re-inserts the typed URL as plain text into the document body at the stray caret — user-visible document content corruption and the exact bug this change claims to fix.
